column5: Six features write to localStorage directly and logout clears only two of the keys so prior user data survives sign out
column6: CLAUDE.md section 5 states plainly that localStorage must not be written directly because redux-persist owns it. Six modules bypass that with fourteen write sites - src/hooks/useRecentSearches.ts:39 stores the search history under recentSearches - src/services/adTrackingService.ts:41 and :45 store ad tracking state - src/pages/shopping-list/index.tsx:103 :109 :115 and :121 store the shopping list keywords - src/components/Modals/DeepLinkModal.tsx:113 :128 :182 and :199 store four app-install flags - src/components/Functional/CookieConsent.tsx:28 and :33 store the consent choice - and src/components/Functional/FirebaseInitializer.tsx:107 stores the FCM token. Because none of this is in the persist store the logout path has to clean up by hand and it does so incompletely - handleLogout at src/helpers/auth.ts:658-659 removes only shoppingListActiveKeywordString and shoppingListKeywords. Everything else survives sign out including the previous account search history and ad tracking state and the FCM token that identifies the device to the push service.
column10: Shared or public device where one account signs out and another signs in - a library machine or a shared family browser or a demo device.
column11: 1. Sign in and use the site so recent searches and ad tracking entries accumulate. 2. Sign out through the account menu. 3. Read localStorage and open the search bar as the next user.
column12: Signing out clears everything tied to the previous session - which is what routing this state through redux-persist would give automatically since its store is purged on logout.
column13: Only the two shopping list keys are removed. The previous account search history remains visible in the search bar to the next user and the ad tracking state and FCM token remain on the device.
column14: The next person to use the device sees what the previous account searched for which is a direct privacy leak on shared machines. The stale FCM token can also keep the device associated with the signed-out account for push delivery.
column15: Move this state into redux-persist slices so the existing purge on logout covers it - that is what the documented rule is for. Where a value genuinely must outlive the session such as the cookie consent choice keep it in localStorage deliberately and document the exception - then extend handleLogout to clear every remaining session-scoped key rather than the two it knows about.

column5: The share landing route re-implements the product page server logic and has drifted from it so a removed product returns a soft 404
column6: src/pages/share/products/[slug].tsx re-exports the product page component at :45 but supplies its own getServerSideProps at :9-43 rather than reusing the canonical one. The two have diverged. The product page checks the fetch result and returns notFound: true when no product came back - src/pages/products/[slug]/index.tsx:324-335 - while the share route returns props unconditionally at :27-33 with no such check. A share link to a deleted or invalid product therefore answers 200 with an empty product page rather than 404. The props type permits it because initialProduct is declared optional at :33 of the product page so nothing fails loudly. The share route also omits country_iso2 which the canonical route reads with getCountryIso2FromContext and passes into the same fetch at :294 and :306 so the delivery estimate that depends on it is absent for every visitor arriving through a share link. Line 43 also carries an undefined as any cast which is the issue 11 class.
column10: A share link pointing at a product that has since been deleted or unpublished or a share link with a malformed slug.
column11: 1. Share a product link so it points at /share/products/{slug}/. 2. Delete or unpublish that product. 3. Open the share link and inspect the HTTP status and the rendered page.
column12: The route behaves exactly like the canonical product page - 404 for a missing product and the same delivery estimate for a present one.
column13: The response is 200 with an empty product page and no delivery estimate is shown even when the product exists.
column14: Soft 404s from share links get indexed and accumulate as thin duplicate pages - and share traffic which is by nature first-time visitor traffic sees a degraded product page missing the delivery information the canonical page shows. Duplicated server logic will keep drifting every time the canonical route changes.
column15: Export the product page getServerSideProps and reuse it from the share route rather than maintaining a second copy - or at minimum add the notFound guard and pass country_iso2 so the two match today. Reusing it also removes the undefined as any cast.
